title: Tehama on I-5 in California: Exit 636 Guide
meta: Tehama sits about 5 miles east of I-5 exit 636. Learn about the town, nearby Thomes Creek, and the closest rest areas in each direction.
intro: Exit 636 (Tehama, Los Molinos, Gyle Road) leads about 5 miles east to the little city of Tehama on the Sacramento River, home to 435 people in 2020. It was the first county seat of Tehama County in 1856, before an election moved the seat to Red Bluff the next year. This stretch is the northern end of a band of farmland that runs almost unbroken to Bakersfield.

faq.q: What exit is Tehama on I-5?
faq.a: Tehama is reached from exit 636, labeled Tehama, Los Molinos, Gyle Road. The town itself is about 5 miles east of the freeway, on the Sacramento River.

faq.q: Why is Tehama called the first county seat?
faq.a: When Tehama County was formed in 1856, Tehama was its county seat. A county-wide election moved the seat to Red Bluff the very next year.

faq.q: Where is the nearest rest area to Tehama on I-5?
faq.a: South of Tehama, the Lt. John C. Helmick Rest Area is at mile 632.2, about 3.8 miles from here, serving both directions. North of town, the Herbert S. Miles Rest Area is at mile 654.1, about 18.1 miles away, also serving both directions.

faq.q: What is Thomes Creek on I-5 near Tehama?
faq.a: The freeway crosses Thomes Creek near exit 633. It is named for Robert Thomes, a pioneer who arrived in the 1840s.
